A Sanskrit manuscript was obtained from the hand of the great master of the <term>Mandala</term> <gloss>sacred circle</gloss>, Chodrak Palzangpo. Based on his command to restore the missing parts and translate the conclusion, the following sections were completed:

In the tenth <term>bampo</term> <gloss>section or volume</gloss>, from the line "Accomplishing all the purposes of activities" until the line "Performing the supreme recitation of the secret mantra."

In the twelfth <term>bampo</term>, from the line "Blessed One, however, for the sake of a special purpose" until the line "The body of the <term>vidyadhara</term> <gloss>knowledge-holder</gloss> will become ablaze."

In the thirteenth <term>bampo</term>, from the line "Merely hearing this ritual of the mandala" until the line "One should carve it to the height of a man."

In the fourteenth <term>bampo</term>, from the line "Having fully empowered the lotus, water, and white mustard seeds with recitations" until the line "One should wash with a white cloth seven times."

At the junction of the fourteenth and fifteenth <term>bampo</term>, from the line "Eight silver incense burners" until the line "In all other various places, one performs all the activities as they are intended."

<summary>This page documents the editorial history of a Tantric text, noting specific passages translated and restored from a Sanskrit manuscript provided by the master Chodrak Palzangpo. It lists the precise starting and ending phrases for additions made across the tenth through fifteenth sections of the work.</summary>
<keywords>Chodrak Palzangpo, Sanskrit manuscript, translation history, bampo, mantra recitation, mandala ritual, vidyadhara</keywords>
